value.text: {"result": {"suggestions": [{"kind": "new_thesis", "ticker": "MSFT", "statement": "Security attach through Microsoft 365 E5 and the E5 Security add-on becomes a source of revenue per user growth in the productivity suite, one that also displaces third-party endpoint and identity vendors and is separate from AI assistant pricing.", "wrong_if": "Reported E5 or E5 Security add-on penetration stops rising, upgraders' revenue per user uplift fades, or EA renewal discounting widens.", "driver_ids": ["MSFT.productivity_growth"], "rationale": "First-hand channel checks show rising E5 penetration, vendor retirement among upgraders and a higher revenue per user with stable discounting, a security-driven upsell debate that none of the pillars covers (p2 is limited to paid AI assistants).", "claim_ids": ["synthetic_000335.c1", "synthetic_000335.c2", "synthetic_000335.c3", "synthetic_000335.c4"], "sections": [{"email_id": "synthetic_000335", "quote": "Tenants with Microsoft 365 E5 or the E5 Security add-on: 31% of the panel, up from 26% in March and 22% a year ago."}, {"email_id": "synthetic_000335", "quote": "Among tenants that moved to E5 or the add-on in the last 12 months, 44% retired at least one third-party endpoint or identity product within 6 months."}, {"email_id": "synthetic_000335", "quote": "Average revenue per user among upgraders rose 19-24%, depending on the starting SKU, before any negotiated discounts."}, {"email_id": "synthetic_000335", "quote": "Renewal-cohort discounting did not widen: median discount off list on EA renewals in the panel was 14%, vs. 15% a year ago."}]}], "no_change_reason": null}}
